key_insight: Chemical reaction models use endpoint-orthogonal latent updates—termed emergent steering—that contribute substantially to predictions beyond movement toward the encoded target.
engineering_relevance: Auditing latent update directions can reveal model failures and bond-edit behavior that endpoint accuracy alone misses.
method: Unify forward prediction and retrosynthesis as direction-conditioned endpoint redistribution in a shared latent space.
Decompose source-to-transformed latent updates into endpoint-parallel movement and an orthogonal steering residual.
Evaluate each component with controls, decoder-interface calibration, and a second graph-edit architecture.
evidence_signal: In retrosynthesis, steering recovers most model utility, affects promoted or suppressed bond edits, and outperforms the parallel component across multiple controls and evaluation settings.
watch_item: The measured steering magnitude depends on the reference axis and optimization, so the decomposition should not be treated as a unique chemical mechanism.
paper_title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models
